item.text: I’m looking for the next refactor that actually simplifies the code instead of just moving pieces around. The strongest remaining cleanup is to make traversal a first-class, reusable internal capability and let list/string rendering build on that, while also removing some now-redundant helper layers around fixtures and expectations.

I found a cleaner seam: the sample/fixture data can carry its own expected outcomes instead of spreading those expectations across `BTreeSamples` and `BTreeTest`. I’m introducing a small scenario object and rewiring the demo/tests to consume it, which should remove the last bit of duplicated sample knowledge.
I’m moving the sample definitions onto that new scenario type now. That lets the fixtures own both the inserted keys and the expected traversal/membership outcomes in one place.
Next I’m simplifying `Main` and the tests to consume scenarios directly. That should remove the remaining duplicated expected-key lists and hard-coded membership checks scattered across the suite.

I found one last bit of duplication while wiring the scenarios in: the bulk-insert test still hard-coded the degree and keys. I’m exposing those from the scenario object so the tests can stay fully data-driven.
The scenario refactor is complete. I’m compiling and rerunning the demo and tests now to verify that the new data-driven fixture layer didn’t change behavior or introduce accidental API mismatches.

Refactored the sample/fixture layer into a single scenario model so the inserted keys, expected traversal, and membership expectations live together instead of being split across helpers and tests. [BTreeScenario.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTreeScenario.java:4) now owns that data and can build a tree directly, while [BTreeSamples.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTreeSamples.java:3) is reduced to named reusable scenarios.

That let me simplify both the demo and the tests. [Main.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/Main.java:2) now consumes the default scenario instead of hard-coding lookup keys, and [BTreeTestSupport.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTreeTestSupport.java:35) can validate an entire scenario in one place. As a result, [BTreeTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/046_b_tree/BTreeTest.java:23) reads more like a set of scenario checks and no longer duplicates sorted-key or membership expectations.
